cards.title: Four patterns, not one
cards.body: At C1 the question is no longer whether you can report what somebody said, but whether you pick the reporting verb whose pattern says exactly what you mean — and then get that pattern right. Four shapes cover almost everything. A verb may take the bare -ing form (she admitted taking it), a to-infinitive with or without a person first (he offered to drive, they warned us not to touch), a that-clause (she claimed that it was wrong), or a preposition and then -ing (he accused her of lying). The pattern belongs to the verb, not to the meaning: suggest and recommend mean nearly what advise means, and take a different pattern from it. That is the whole difficulty, and the reason this unit is a list to be learnt rather than a rule to be applied.
cards.body_cz: Na úrovni C1 už nejde o to, zda dokážete sdělit, co někdo řekl, ale zda zvolíte sloveso, jehož vazba řekne přesně to, co míníte — a zda tu vazbu pak utvoříte správně. Téměř vše pokryjí čtyři tvary. Sloveso může mít holý tvar -ing (she admitted taking it), infinitiv s to s osobou nebo bez ní (he offered to drive, they warned us not to touch), vedlejší větu s that (she claimed that it was wrong), anebo předložku a po ní -ing (he accused her of lying). Vazba patří ke slovesu, nikoli k významu: suggest a recommend znamenají téměř totéž co advise, a mají jinou vazbu než ono. V tom je celá obtížnost a proto je tato lekce seznamem k naučení, nikoli pravidlem k použití.

points: The pattern is a fact about the verb and has to be learnt with it.

cards.title: The bare -ing family
cards.body: Admit, deny, suggest, recommend, propose, mention, acknowledge, regret, report and advise take the -ing form with nothing in front of it. The Czech behind these sentences is nearly always a že-clause, so there is no -ing in the sentence you start from, and the infinitive suggests itself instead. Suggest and recommend are the two worst offenders, because navrhnout and doporučit take a Czech infinitive: she suggested to postpone the meeting is a calque and is wrong, and so is he recommended me to wait. Repair them either with -ing (she suggested postponing) or with a that-clause (she suggested that we postpone). Admit and confess also allow to plus -ing, which is a preposition and not an infinitive: he admitted to taking it.
cards.body_cz: Slovesa admit, deny, suggest, recommend, propose, mention, acknowledge, regret, report a advise mají tvar -ing bez čehokoli před ním. Čeština za těmito větami má téměř vždy větu se spojkou že, takže ve výchozí větě žádné -ing není a nabízí se infinitiv. Nejhůře dopadají suggest a recommend, protože navrhnout a doporučit se pojí s českým infinitivem: she suggested to postpone the meeting je kalk a je chybné, stejně jako he recommended me to wait. Opravíte je buď tvarem -ing (she suggested postponing), nebo větou s that (she suggested that we postpone). Admit a confess připouštějí také to plus -ing, kde to je předložka, nikoli infinitiv: he admitted to taking it.

cards.title: The to-infinitive family, with and without a person
cards.title_cz: Skupina s infinitivem, s osobou i bez ní
cards.body: Promise, offer, refuse, threaten, claim and agree go straight to the infinitive: he offered to drive us. Advise, warn, remind, urge, persuade, encourage, tell, ask and order need a person in between: she reminded him to lock the door. Nothing about the meaning tells you which group a verb is in, and a verb from one group put into the other is simply ungrammatical. The negative is the other thing to get right: it goes before to, so they warned us not to touch the wires. To not touch is a marked form that draws attention to itself and does not belong in careful writing. Note that warn appears in three patterns — warn somebody not to do it, warn somebody against doing it, and warn somebody that something is true — all three correct and all three common.
cards.body_cz: Slovesa promise, offer, refuse, threaten, claim a agree míří přímo k infinitivu: he offered to drive us. Slovesa advise, warn, remind, urge, persuade, encourage, tell, ask a order potřebují mezi sebe a infinitiv osobu: she reminded him to lock the door. Nic ve významu neprozradí, do které skupiny sloveso patří, a sloveso z jedné skupiny použité podle druhé je prostě negramatické. Druhá věc je zápor: stojí před to, tedy they warned us not to touch the wires. Tvar to not touch je příznakový, upozorňuje sám na sebe a do pečlivého psaní nepatří. Všimněte si, že warn má tři vazby — warn somebody not to do it, warn somebody against doing it a warn somebody that something is true — a všechny tři jsou správné a běžné.

cards.title: The that-clause family, and the base form inside it
cards.title_cz: Skupina s větou s that a základní tvar v ní
cards.body: Verbs that simply report — claim, argue, point out, explain, complain, announce, admit, deny — take an ordinary tense in the that-clause, with the usual backshift: she claimed that the report was wrong. Verbs of demanding are different. Insist, demand, recommend, suggest, propose and request take the bare base form, the mandative subjunctive from the previous unit: he insisted that we leave immediately, she demanded that the money be returned. No third-person -s appears, and be is the form for every person. British English also allows should here — insisted that we should leave — and that is worth knowing because it is the form a Czech learner is most likely to have been taught.
cards.body_cz: Slovesa, která pouze sdělují — claim, argue, point out, explain, complain, announce, admit, deny — mají ve větě s that běžný čas a platí obvyklé posouvání časů: she claimed that the report was wrong. Slovesa žádosti jsou jiná. Insist, demand, recommend, suggest, propose a request mají holý základní tvar, tedy mandativní konjunktiv z předchozí lekce: he insisted that we leave immediately, she demanded that the money be returned. Koncovka třetí osoby se neobjeví a be je tvarem pro všechny osoby. Britská angličtina zde připouští i should — insisted that we should leave — a stojí za to to vědět, protože právě tento tvar český student nejčastěji zná ze školy.

table.caption: reporting versus demanding
rows: She claimed that the report was wrong.
He insisted that we leave immediately.
He argued that the plan would fail.
She demanded that the money be returned.

They recommended that the office move.

The negative in the demanding pattern is a bare not: that he not be told.
A past reporting verb does not change the base form: it was vital that he arrive.

cards.title: Verb, person, preposition, -ing
cards.body: The last family fixes a preposition between the person and the action, and the preposition is a property of the verb that no rule predicts. Accuse somebody of, suspect somebody of, congratulate somebody on, insist on, blame somebody for, criticise somebody for, thank somebody for, apologise for, confess to, object to, warn somebody against, prevent somebody from, discourage somebody from. Because these are prepositions, what follows is the -ing form: he accused her of hiding it, never of to hide it. The Czech preposition is no help whatever — obvinit z gives of, poděkovat za gives for, blahopřát k gives on, zabránit v gives from — so each pair has to be learnt whole.
cards.body_cz: Poslední skupina klade mezi osobu a děj předložku a ta je vlastností slovesa, kterou žádné pravidlo nepředpoví. Accuse somebody of, suspect somebody of, congratulate somebody on, insist on, blame somebody for, criticise somebody for, thank somebody for, apologise for, confess to, object to, warn somebody against, prevent somebody from, discourage somebody from. Protože jde o předložky, následuje tvar -ing: he accused her of hiding it, nikoli of to hide it. Česká předložka nepomůže vůbec — obvinit z dává of, poděkovat za dává for, blahopřát k dává on, zabránit v dává from — a proto je třeba se každou dvojici naučit vcelku.

table.caption: the preposition is fixed by the verb
rows: přiznat se k / ohradit se proti

points: To in confess to and object to is a preposition, so -ing follows: object to paying.
Accuse of and blame for describe the same event from two angles; they are not interchangeable.
Apologise takes for and no object: apologise to somebody for doing something.

cards.title: Say, tell, and the errors that survive to C1
cards.title_cz: Say, tell a chyby, které přežijí do C1
cards.body: A small set of errors outlives everything else, because the sentence still reads and nobody corrects it. Say takes no person unless you add to: he said to me, never he said me. Tell requires one: he told me, never he told that. Explain and describe behave like say and take to — he explained to me that, because čeština says vysvětlil mi and the dative slides straight into English as an object. Finally, some verbs take two patterns with two meanings, and these are worth memorising as pairs: he remembered locking the door reports a memory of the act, he remembered to lock it reports that he did not forget; she stopped smoking gave it up, she stopped to smoke paused in order to.
cards.body_cz: Malá skupina chyb přežije vše ostatní, protože věta i tak dává smysl a nikdo ji neopravuje. Say se nepojí s osobou, dokud nepřidáte to: he said to me, nikdy he said me. Tell osobu vyžaduje: he told me, nikdy he told that. Explain a describe se chovají jako say a pojí se s to — he explained to me that — protože čeština říká vysvětlil mi a český dativ se do angličtiny přenáší jako předmět. Některá slovesa mají dvě vazby a s nimi dva významy a ty se vyplatí pamatovat si ve dvojicích: he remembered locking the door sděluje vzpomínku na samý čin, he remembered to lock it sděluje, že nezapomněl; she stopped smoking znamená, že přestala kouřit, she stopped to smoke, že se zastavila, aby si zakouřila.

table.caption: the ones that survive
rows: He said me that it was late.
He said to me that it was late.
He told that it was late.
He told me that it was late.
She explained the rule to me.

points: Two patterns, two meanings: remember doing versus remember to do; stop doing versus stop to do.
Regret doing looks back; regret to inform announces bad news now.
Deny takes -ing or a that-clause, but never a to-infinitive.

items.gap: She admitted ____ the file.
accepts: She admitted taking the file.

Nástraha pro Čecha je v tom, že český originál má téměř vždy vedlejší větu se spojkou že — přiznala, že vzala spis — takže ve větě, z níž překládáte, žádné -ing není a nabízí se místo něj infinitiv. The trap for a Czech speaker is that the Czech original is almost always a že-clause — přiznala, že vzala spis — so there is no -ing anywhere in the sentence you are translating from, and the infinitive offers itself instead. Suggest and recommend are the two that are got wrong most often, because their Czech equivalents navrhnout and doporučit take an infinitive: she suggested to postpone the meeting is a straight calque and is wrong. Admit and confess additionally allow a preposition — admit to taking, confess to taking — but the bare -ing is always available and is the safer form.

items.explanation: The second family takes a to-infinitive. Some of these verbs go straight to it — promise, offer, refuse, threaten, claim, agree — and some need a person first: advise somebody to, warn somebody not to, remind somebody to, urge somebody to, persuade somebody to, encourage somebody to. Which of the two shapes a verb takes is a fact about that verb and has to be learnt with it; there is no rule that predicts it. Two errors are worth naming. Suggest and recommend never join this family — he suggested me to wait is wrong for both, and the repair is he suggested that I wait or he suggested waiting. And the negative goes in front of the to, not after it: they warned us not to touch the machine. To not touch is not the neutral form and does not belong in careful writing.
items.explanation_cz: Druhá skupina se pojí s infinitivem s to. Některá z těchto sloves k němu míří přímo — promise, offer, refuse, threaten, claim, agree — a některá potřebují nejprve osobu: advise somebody to, warn somebody not to, remind somebody to, urge somebody to, persuade somebody to, encourage somebody to. To, kterou z obou vazeb sloveso má, je vlastností toho slovesa a je třeba se ji naučit s ním; žádné pravidlo ji nepředpoví. Dvě chyby stojí za pojmenování. Suggest a recommend do této skupiny nikdy nepatří — he suggested me to wait je u obou chybné a správně je he suggested that I wait nebo he suggested waiting. A zápor stojí před to, nikoli za ním: they warned us not to touch the machine. Tvar to not touch není neutrální a do pečlivého psaní nepatří.
